notes: Implement-from-scratch. The naive `for c in s: if s.count(c) == 1: return c` is correct but O(n^2). The O(n) answer is a frequency map (Counter / dict) then a single scan. check.py verifies correctness on edge cases + a large randomized input vs a reference, then runs the shared complexity probe (tasks/_optimality.py): FAIL if runtime scales super-linearly. Companion to 038 (dedupe).
